title: Proteomic Biomarkers for Bisphenol A-Early Exposure and Women's Thyroid Cancer.
ehr_evidence: Matched pairs of thyroid tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues were collected from women thyroid cancer patients (n=28; age, 47.4±11.6 years; papillary carcinoma, 100%; metasatasis, 10.4% of the subjects), who received a surgical treatment at Hanyang University Hospital, Seoul, Korea.
summary: Experimental study using in utero BPA-exposed mice and human thyroid tissue samples to identify proteomic biomarkers associated with early-life BPA exposure and women's thyroid cancer.
key_findings: 17 proteins were altered in a dose-dependent manner in mouse thyroid tissues following prenatal BPA exposure.
No significant differences were found in mRNA expression of ANXA6, ATP5B, HSPA5, or VCP between tumor and adjacent non-tumor thyroid tissues in women (p > 0.05).
Blood BPA was detected in 90% of thyroid cancer patients (range 0-10.32 ng/mL).

Strong positive associations were observed between blood BPA levels and mRNA expression of VCP (r2=0.47, p=0.02) and ANXA6 (r2=0.37, p=0.03) specifically in thyroid tumor tissues, but not in normal tissues.
captured_features: mRNA expression of ANXA6, ATP5B, HSPA5, VCP
thyroid tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues
study_design: In utero animal exposure study with ex vivo human tissue validation
population: Female ICR mice offspring and women with papillary thyroid cancer (n=28, mean age 47.4 years)
limitations: small sample size of human tissues (n=28)
